issue_context.title: API Proposal: Import keys from RFC7468 PEM
comments:
It might make more sense to be error if

* Two(+) "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY" units are found
* Two(+) "BEGIN [this kind of] KEY" units are found
* One(+) each of "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY" and "BEGIN [this kind of] KEY" units are found.

That way it doesn't hit future algorithm errors on upgrade.  (It won't crack the PKCS#8, just the mere presence raises contention)

Presumably there should be a sister method group for EncryptedPkcs8?

And, nitpicky, you forgot ECDH :)

@bartonjs 

>It might make more sense to be error if blah

I like your suggestion. For completeness, a BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY will count as a BEGIN PRIVATE KEY.

>Presumably there should be a sister method group for EncryptedPkcs8?

Added.

>And, nitpicky, you forgot ECDH :)

Bah. Added.

I was waffling on "BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY" counting or not.  I'm cool with being conservative and counting it (so an error for both "BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY" and "BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY", but also an error for only "BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY", unless that's supposed to try reading it with the null and empty passwords...)

> unless that's supposed to try reading it with the null and empty passwords...

I hadn't planned on that. While that seems doable there is a lack of explicitness there that I personally don't care for.

> here is a lack of explicitness there that I personally don't care for.

I concur.  But that's why I was on the fence of whether or not it would count as making the input "ambiguous" :)

@bartonjs 

I'm almost done with this and am working through the XML docs. I do have a question about it: since these methods will ultimately use other public and documented import methods as the workhorse, how do exceptions get documented? Is it expected that every exception `ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo` can throw also gets documented on `ImportFromPem`? Is there a way to say "and see these other methods for all the things it can throw?"

> Is it expected that every exception ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo can throw also gets documented on ImportFromPem

I believe so, that's what I've been doing, at least.

Adding a `<seealso cref="whatever"/>` has goodness, but I don't think there's an "import these exceptions"

Of course, you could decide to say `<exception cref="CryptographicException">An error occurred during key import.</exception>`.  But consider the quality of docs you'd like to read while doing the "::sigh:: boilerplate documentation" shortcuts :smile:.

review_comments:
On the one hand, it seems like we could have the base class version support SPKI and PKCS8; but since everything except DSA has defined their own specific private key format as a top-level item, I agree that everything would probably end up overriding it anyways.

The encrypted ones seem less convincing... I think we can provide default implementations of those.

@bartonjs one problem with pulling the implementation in to `AsymmetricAlgorithm`: `AsymmetricAlgorithm` lives in S.S.C.Primitives while the algorithm base classes live in S.S.C.Algorithms. S.S.C.Algorithms references S.S.C.Encoding, where `PemEncoding` lives. Primitives cannot make that reference, because Encoding references Primitives, and we can't have circular references.

Thoughts?
Fair enough.  I'll accept "dependencies" as a good reason why it can't have a default implementation.  If we move the class around perhaps we'll remember to come fill this in.

Encrypted followed by plain reports ambiguous, plain followed by encrypted reports encrypted.

It seems like either this branch, or the match on the label, should notice that `importAction` is not null, and report ambiguous.

Is it ambiguous on an RSA key for `EC PRIVATE KEY` and `RSA PRIVATE KEY`? What about `EC PRIVATE KEY` and `PRIVATE KEY` (whether or not the PKCS#8 has the RSA Oid)?

I'm not sure I actually care what the answer is, but I'd like to see a "not contextually applicable" format test that used a known-as-a-key-type format.

We touched a bit on this in the original issue, the gist is:

1. For PKCS8/SPKI keys, we don't decode them for purposes of reporting a duplicate. If a PKCS1 and PKCS8 PEM are found, we assume dupe, even in the PKCS8 turns out to be a key for an entirely different algorithm.
2. If the labels are for two known-to-be-not-ambiguous keys, like EC PRIVATE KEY and RSA PRIVATE KEY, we won't report a duplicate. I think the rationale there was that we don't have a crystal ball for future algorithms. If we throw ambiguous for EC PRIVATE KEY for example while importing RSA, and eventually .NET gets enlightened with a new algorithm with PEM encoding (say ED25519 since it doesn't use the regular "EC" label), we wouldn't want to start breaking people's existing PEM aggregates that contained those algorithms we once ignored.
Yep, those both sound reasonable (and what I felt the conclusions had been); I'm after the test that proves it for "known key types" vs "this algorithm's known key types" :smile:
Regardless I will illustrate this better with tests.

I assume that you've made a conscious choice to say it's OK to ignore trailing bytes here, since there's no check that the import action reports bytesRead == base64Size.

I can accept that... but a comment saying so would be nice.  (Reasonable justification includes that the key has already been modified, so throwing and not have the same object modification effect)
Since ImportEncryptedPkcs8PrivateKey comes from AsymmetricAlgorithm, why do all of the key types need to implement this method?  Seems like it could just be the virtual implementation...

@bartonjs that's a good point. [The API proposal][1] had all of them overriden. If we remove the `override`s from the RSA/DSA/ECDsa, do we need to go through another round of API Review?

[1]: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/31201#issue-558482299
Nah, from the pure API perspective it was only the `virtual` that was interesting.  Removing overrides that don't yet actually exist is just an implementation detail.
I'd probably just cut the sentence.  Assuming it's mirroring what I wrote on ImportPkcs8PrivateKey (assuming I wrote something like that), I was just saying "this doesn't understand PEM" :)
